faq.q: Is it dangerous to use a gas stove with an ignition problem?
faq.a: If you smell gas when the burner fails to light, stop using the stove, ventilate the area, and call us. If the burner simply clicks without lighting and there's no gas odor, the issue is typically a dirty igniter or misaligned burner cap — still worth fixing promptly, but not an emergency.

faq.q: What's the difference between a range, a stove, and a cooktop?
faq.a: A range combines a cooktop and oven in a single unit. A stove is a general term that usually refers to the cooktop portion. A cooktop is a standalone unit built into the counter without an oven below it. We repair all three types.

faq.q: My range's oven heats unevenly — one side burns while the other undercoooks. Why?
faq.a: Uneven heating is typically caused by a failing convection fan (if equipped), a warped bake element, or a drifting oven sensor. In some cases, the range isn't level, which causes hot air to circulate unevenly. We check all possibilities during the diagnostic.

faq.q: How long do gas range igniters last?
faq.a: Most gas igniters last 8-12 years with normal use. If your range takes noticeably longer to light than it did when new, the igniter is weakening and should be replaced proactively — it's an inexpensive part and a quick repair.

garbage-disposal-repair-and-installation.repairTips: Always run cold water for 15 seconds before and after using your garbage disposal — cold water solidifies grease so it can be chopped up rather than coating your Naperville home's drain pipes. Feed waste gradually instead of stuffing the chamber, and avoid fibrous foods like celery stalks or corn husks that wrap around the impellers. If your disposal hums but won't grind, try the reset button on the bottom of the unit before calling — it's a built-in breaker that trips during jams and resolves about 20% of the service calls we receive in Naperville.

faq.q: My garbage disposal hums but won't grind. Do I need a new one?
faq.a: Not necessarily. A humming disposal is usually jammed — something is stuck between the impellers and the grinding ring. Press the reset button on the bottom, then try the hex wrench in the manual rotation socket. If that doesn't free it, our technician can clear the jam. A new unit is only needed if the motor itself has burned out.

faq.q: What size garbage disposal do Naperville homes typically need?
faq.a: For a household of 2-4 people who cook regularly, a 3/4 HP disposal handles daily use comfortably. Larger families or avid cooks benefit from a 1 HP unit. The 1/3 HP disposals that builders install in many Naperville homes are underpowered for most families.

faq.q: How long does a garbage disposal installation take in Naperville?

faq.q: My washer leaves clothes soaking wet after the spin cycle. What's wrong?
faq.a: The most common causes are a failed lid switch (top-loaders), worn shock absorbers causing the tub to hit the off-balance switch (front-loaders), a clogged drain pump, or a broken drive coupler. We test each during the diagnostic and carry replacement parts for all of them.

faq.q: My Aurora refrigerator stopped cooling after a power outage. Is the compressor dead?
faq.a: Not always. Power surges when electricity is restored often damage the compressor start relay — a far less expensive component than the compressor itself. We test the relay first, which resolves a significant percentage of post-outage cooling failures without a major repair.

faq.q: How can I protect my refrigerator from Aurora's summer storms?
faq.a: Plug it into a surge protector rated for large appliances (not a standard power strip). This shields the compressor and electronic controls from the voltage spikes that occur when power is restored after an outage. It's an inexpensive precaution that prevents costly repairs.

faq.q: My refrigerator's ice maker stopped working but everything else is fine. What's wrong?
faq.a: Common causes include a frozen water supply line, a failed water inlet valve, a defective ice maker module, or a freezer temperature that's slightly too warm for ice production. We carry parts for all four scenarios and can usually resolve the issue in one visit.

faq.q: Is it worth repairing a 15-year-old refrigerator in Aurora?

faq.q: The gas burners on my stove light unevenly — some strong, some weak. Why?

faq.q: Can you fix an induction cooktop in Aurora?

faq.q: The oven in my range doesn't match the temperature I set. How far off is normal?
faq.a: Most manufacturers allow a +/- 25°F variance. If your oven is consistently off by more than that, the oven sensor has likely drifted and needs replacement. We test with calibrated instruments during the diagnostic and can recalibrate or replace on the spot.

faq.q: Can you repair a slide-in range without pulling it completely out of the cabinet opening?

faq.q: My range's self-clean cycle locked the door and now it won't open. What do I do?

Never pour cooking grease or oil down the disposal; it solidifies in Aurora's older cast-iron drain lines and creates stubborn blockages. faq.q: My Aurora home has never had a garbage disposal. Can you install one?

faq.q: The builder installed a 1/3 HP disposal in my new Aurora home and it can't handle our family's use. What do you recommend?

faq.q: My disposal leaks from the bottom. Is it repairable?
faq.a: A leak from the very bottom of the unit usually indicates a failed internal seal around the motor shaft — at that point, replacement is more cost-effective than repair. A leak from the flange connection at the top or the discharge elbow on the side is typically repairable by re-sealing or tightening the connection.

faq.q: Can you work on a disposal connected to a septic system in Aurora?
faq.a: Yes, though we recommend using the disposal sparingly on septic systems. Ground food waste increases the solid load in the septic tank, requiring more frequent pumping. We can install a disposal and advise on usage practices that minimize the impact on your septic system.

dryer-repair.repairTips: Check your exterior dryer vent hood during Joliet's coldest stretches — ice buildup on the flap is a common cause of sudden heating failure in winter. If your dryer is in a basement, ensure the vent doesn't sag or dip along its run; low points collect moisture and lint that restrict airflow. Schedule a professional vent cleaning every 12 months, or every 6 months if your household does more than seven loads per week. Replace any vinyl or foil vent ducting with rigid metal — it's required by current code and significantly reduces fire risk.

faq.q: My Joliet dryer stopped heating suddenly during a cold snap. What happened?
faq.a: In Joliet's winter temperatures, moisture in the dryer exhaust can freeze the exterior vent flap shut, blocking airflow entirely. This causes the dryer to overheat and trip the thermal fuse — a safety device that shuts off the heating circuit. We replace the fuse, clear the vent, and verify airflow before we leave.

faq.q: How often should dryer vents be cleaned in Joliet homes?
faq.a: Annually at minimum. Joliet's older homes with long basement vent runs should consider every 6-9 months, especially if the household does heavy laundry volume. Lint buildup is invisible inside the duct and is a documented fire hazard.

faq.q: My dryer makes a loud thumping sound. Is it safe to use?
faq.a: Thumping usually indicates worn drum support rollers or a loose baffle inside the drum. It's not immediately dangerous, but the noise will worsen and the failing component can eventually damage the drum or shaft. It's best to have it repaired soon.
